policies.title: Paraguay: named ordinary passports visa-free for tourist entry
policies.summary: The National Migration Directorate's current country table directly marks these nationalities 'NO REQUIERE VISA' in its tourist-entry column. This is a visa exemption, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The authority’s table is used only for nationalities it explicitly names and only for its tourist-entry column. No residual status is inferred from a missing row, generic application form, agreement label or a third-country document.
Where stated in the table, the tourist stay is up to 30, 60 or 90 days; the source does not provide a single shared duration for this entire cohort, so no uniform duration is assigned.

The separate entry-requirements page retains valid travel-document, migration-registration, admission and other border conditions. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes are outside this ordinary short-visitor baseline.

Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the United States are deliberately not included: the migration table says visa-free while the Foreign Ministry’s current arrival page names them for visa on arrival. Taiwan has the same cross-source disagreement. Mongolia is also excluded because the Foreign Ministry’s country-requirements page states that unlisted countries require a visa, but it does not list Mongolia.

policies.title: Paraguay: named ordinary passports visa on arrival
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry expressly says these nationalities can obtain a visa on arrival at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport without prior processing, on presentation of a qualifying passport and payment of the fee. This is visa_on_arrival, not an eVisa or ETA.
conditions: The named route is at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport and requires a passport valid for at least six months and payment of the applicable fee.

The National Migration Directorate separately marks these same nationalities as requiring a visa in its tourist-entry column; the Foreign Ministry's direct arrival-issuance page supplies the more specific route classification.

The exceptional arrival process for other visa-required nationalities requires a justified case, an inviter and advance Ministry review; it is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival entitlement and is excluded.
Work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Paraguay: named ordinary passports require an advance visitor visa
policies.summary: The National Migration Directorate's current tourist-entry table directly marks these nationalities 'REQUIERE VISA', except that the Foreign Ministry's current country-requirements page supplies the explicit unlisted-country visa rule for China. The Foreign Ministry describes the regular consular application and treats arrival issuance for other visa-required nationalities as exceptional and pre-approved; this is normalized as visa_required, not eVisa or a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The regular route is an online application reviewed by the relevant Paraguayan consular office, followed by the Ministry's communicated consular appointment. An online form does not establish an eVisa.

The National Migration Directorate's combined 'China/Taiwan' row cannot safely be used for the People's Republic of China code. The Foreign Ministry instead expressly lists Taiwan as visa-free and says an unlisted country requires a visa, establishing the China code's advance-visa baseline.

For a visa-required nationality other than the named no-prior-processing arrival cohort, the arrival-visa page characterizes arrival issuance as exceptional, justified and subject to Ministry process and approval. It does not replace this nationality-only advance-visa baseline.
Venezuelan nationals are specifically subject again to a visa requirement from 10 January 2026 under the Foreign Ministry notice, corroborating the current migration table.

No duration, number of entries, fee, extension, accommodation, funds, health, onward-travel or admission outcome is inferred where the authority does not state it. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

application.label: Paraguay Foreign Ministry non-resident tourist/technical visa application
application.processingTime: The Foreign Ministry recommends applying at least 30 days before planned travel; no uniform approval time is promised.
steps: Complete the Foreign Ministry's digital visa application and upload the requested supporting documents.
Wait for the responsible Paraguayan consular office to review the application and communicate any additional documents or an interview appointment.
Obtain the visa through the regular consular process before travel; admission remains for migration authorities at the border.

policies.title: Paraguayan citizens: national return
policies.summary: The National Migration Directorate expressly accepts Paraguayan national travel documents, including an expired national travel document, for entry. The same-country ordinary-passport pair is citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa classification.
conditions: This records only the national entry function. It does not decide document issuance, dual nationality, exit requirements, customs, health, criminal process, security checks or other border formalities.

conflicts.explanation: The National Migration Directorate's current tourist-entry table directly marks the Commonwealth of the Bahamas as not requiring a visa for up to 90 days.
The Foreign Ministry expressly names Qatar among nationalities that can obtain a visa on arrival without prior processing; the migration table also marks Qatar as requiring a visa.
The Foreign Ministry expressly names Thailand for visa on arrival without prior processing; the migration table also marks Thailand as requiring a visa.
The Foreign Ministry expressly names Indonesia for visa on arrival without prior processing; the migration table also marks Indonesia as requiring a visa.
The Foreign Ministry expressly names Vietnam for visa on arrival without prior processing; the migration table also marks Vietnam as requiring a visa.
The current migration table marks Venezuela as requiring a visa, and the Foreign Ministry restored the visa requirement from 10 January 2026.
